376199.title: Lew's higher-dimensional Brouwer Laplacian conjecture
376199.literal_statement:
Let $K$ be an $r$-dimensional simplicial complex, let $f_r(K)$ denote the number of $r$-faces, and let $\lambda_{r-1,i}(K)$ be the eigenvalues of the up-Laplacian on $(r-1)$-faces, arranged in nonincreasing order. **Lew's conjecture.** For every integer $\ell \geq 1$,

$$
\sum_{i = 1}^{\ell}\lambda_{r-1,i}(K) \leq f_r(K) + \binom{\ell}{2} + r\ell.
$$

This is proposed as a higher-dimensional analogue of Brouwer's Laplacian conjecture for graphs. The source does not report a resolution of Lew's conjecture.

376322.title: The dual-cube lifting conjecture for completely independent spanning trees
376322.literal_statement: Let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube and let $F_{n+1}$ be the dual-cube of dimension $n+1$. Let $k$ be a positive integer. **Dual-cube lifting conjecture.** If $Q_n$ has $k$ completely independent spanning trees, then $F_{n+1}$ also has $k$ completely independent spanning trees. The conjecture is motivated by the fact that each cluster of $F_n$ is isomorphic to $Q_{n-1}$ and that the cluster-connecting graph admits edge-disjoint connecting structures. The paper establishes a construction for two completely independent spanning trees, but the asserted implication for arbitrary $k$ remains open.

366543.title: Refinement of the perfect-power repulsion conjecture for partition numbers
366543.literal_statement:
Let $p(n)$ be the partition function, let $\Delta_k(n)$ be the distance from $p(n)$ to the nearest $k$th power, and let

$$
M_k(d):=\max\left\{n:\Delta_k(n)\leq d\right\}.
$$

**Refinement of the perfect-power repulsion conjecture.** If $k>1$, then $M_k(0)=1$, and for every $\varepsilon>0$,

$$
M_k(d)=o\left(d^{\varepsilon}\right).
$$

The first assertion recapitulates Sun's conjecture, while the second gives a sub-polynomial upper bound on the last partition index within distance $d$ of a $k$th power. It is presented as a numerical refinement and remains open.

366579.title: The D-antimagic neighborhood conjecture
366579.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $D\subseteq\{0,1,2,\dots,\operatorname{diam}(G)\}$ be a non-empty distance set, and define the $D$-neighborhood of a vertex $u$ by

$$
N_D(u)=\{v\mid d(v,u)\in D\}.
$$

A bijection $f:V(G)\rightarrow\{0,1,2,\dots,\operatorname{diam}(G)\}$ is a $D$-antimagic labeling when the $D$-weights

$$
\omega_D(u)=\sum_{v\in N_D(u)}f(v)
$$

are distinct for every vertex $u$; in that case $G$ is $D$-antimagic. **The D-antimagic neighborhood conjecture.** A graph $G$ is $D$-antimagic if and only if every vertex in $G$ has a distinct $D$-neighborhood. This generalizes the distance-antimagic claim when $D=\{1\}$; the supplied text does not establish the conjecture beyond presenting it as a proposed generalization.

366639.title: The reversal symmetry conjecture for expected coin-flip ending times
366639.literal_statement:
Let $S$ be a finite ending string of heads and tails, let $S'$ be its reversal, and let $E(S)$ denote the expected number of fair-coin flips needed to produce $S$. Thus, if $S=s_1s_2\cdots s_r$, then $S'=s_rs_{r-1}\cdots s_1$.

**Reversal symmetry conjecture.** If $S'$ is the reversal of an ending string $S$, then

$$
E(S)=E(S').
$$

The paper establishes this symmetry for ending strings with two, three, and four alternating runs through the cited preceding theorems. The conjecture extends that observed symmetry to arbitrary ending strings.

366805.title: Markov polynomial weak log-concavity conjecture
366805.literal_statement: Let $M_\rho$ be a Markov polynomial, and let its coefficients be regarded as weights on the corresponding Newton polygon. A sequence is log-concave when $x_k^2\geq x_{k-1}x_{k+1}$ for every interior index $k$. The weights satisfy weak log-concavity when their sequences in the horizontal, vertical, and diagonal directions with $i+j$ constant are all log-concave. **Log-concavity conjecture.** The coefficients of Markov polynomials are weakly log-concave on the corresponding Newton polygon. This extends the observed coefficient-positivity phenomenon to a directional log-concavity property; the source reports experimental evidence but no proof or resolution.

367031.title: Ultra-log-concavity of weak-order Eulerian polynomials
367031.literal_statement:
Let $\pi\in\mathfrak{S}_n$. The polynomial

$$
Q_W^\pi(t)=\sum_{\sigma\in[\operatorname{id},\pi]_W}t^{\operatorname{des}(\sigma)}
$$

is the weak-order Eulerian polynomial of the interval below $\pi$.

**Ultra-log-concavity conjecture.** For every $\pi\in\mathfrak{S}_n$, $Q_W^\pi$ is ultra-log-concave.

This is a special case of Brenti's conjecture, rephrased in the language of the weak order. The claim is motivated by ultra-log-concavity results for naturally labeled width-two posets, although the corresponding polynomials for general permutation posets need not be real-rooted.

367033.title: The parity conjecture for ensnaring graph complements
367033.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be an $m$-vertex graph. For an integer $n\ge m$, define the **$n$-vertex complement** of $G$, denoted $\operatorname{compl}_n(G)$, to be the $n$-vertex graph whose complement consists of $G$ together with $n-m$ additional isolated vertices. **Parity conjecture for ensnaring complements.** Fix an $m$-vertex graph $G$. Then for all integers $n>m$, whether $\operatorname{compl}_n(G)$ is ensnaring depends only on the parity of $n$.

The conjecture addresses the dependence on the number of added isolated vertices in the $n$-vertex complement. The preceding theorem reduces ensnaring to the corresponding complements of connected components of the graph complement, but the parity dependence for a fixed graph is left open.

367184.title: 1-Rayleigh conjecture for the normalized Kahn–Saks polynomial
367184.literal_statement:
Let $x_1\leq\ldots\leq x_k$ be a chain, let $P_{\mathrm{KS}}$ be its Kahn–Saks polynomial, and let $N(P_{\mathrm{KS}})$ denote its normalization. For exponent vectors $\alpha$ and indices $i,j$, write $\partial^\alpha$ for the corresponding partial derivative. **1-Rayleigh conjecture.** The normalized Kahn–Saks polynomial is $1$-Rayleigh: for every $(u,v)\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq0}^k$,

$$
\partial^\alpha N(P_{\mathrm{KS}})\,\partial^{\alpha+e_i+e_j}N(P_{\mathrm{KS}})(u,v)\leq\partial^{\alpha+e_i}N(P_{\mathrm{KS}})\,\partial^{\alpha+e_j}N(P_{\mathrm{KS}})(u,v).
$$

The conjecture proposes a strong Rayleigh-type inequality for the normalized Kahn–Saks polynomial. The excerpt supplies no resolution, so its status remains open.

367383.title: Jain's connectivity and diameter conjecture for unit graphs over \(\mathbb{Z}_n\)
367383.literal_statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $G(\mathbb{Z}_n)$ be the unit graph. $$
2\in U(\mathbb{Z}_n)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \operatorname{diam}(G(\mathbb{Z}_n))\leq 2,
$$

while

$$
2\in N_U(\mathbb{Z}_n)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \operatorname{diam}(G(\mathbb{Z}_n))\leq 3.
$$

The conjecture concerns the connectivity and metric structure of unit graphs for arbitrary natural $n$. The surrounding paper states that these assertions are resolved there, so this candidate is treated as solved.

367401.title: The Ehrhart–Zeta duality conjecture for linear arbors
367401.literal_statement:
Let $t$ be a **linear arbor**, meaning an arbor in which each vertex has at most one sub-tree. Let $\operatorname{Rev}(t)$ be its reverse, obtained by putting the vertices in the opposite order. Let $Q_t$ be the associated polytope, $E_t(u)$ its Ehrhart polynomial, and $P_t$ its associated poset with Zeta polynomial $Z_t(u)$.

**The Ehrhart–Zeta duality conjecture.** For every linear arbor $t$,

$$
E_t(u)=Z_{\operatorname{Rev}(t)}(u+1).
$$

The conjecture would identify the normalized volume of $Q_t$ with the number of maximal chains of $P_{\operatorname{Rev}(t)}$. The source presents this as open and notes a further expected h-vector symmetry under reversal.

367442.title: Reading's separation conjecture for cluster variables
367442.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a cluster algebra. For cluster variables $u=x_{i;t}$ and $u'=x_{j;t'}$, write $g_{k;u}^s$ and $g_{k;u'}^s$ for the $k$th components of their $g$-vectors at a vertex $s$ of the exchange tree. The variables are **sign-coherent** when

$$
g_{k;u}^s g_{k;u'}^s\geq 0
$$

for every vertex $s$ and every $k\in[1,n]$.

**Reading's separation conjecture.** The variables $u$ and $u'$ are contained in the same cluster if and only if they are sign-coherent.

This reformulates Reading's conjectured separation property for cluster variables in universal geometric cluster algebras. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.

367492.title: The small-set function restricted-sumset conjecture
367492.literal_statement:
Let $p$ be a prime number, and let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p$ satisfy $|B|\leqslant |A|$. Let $\mathcal{R}\colon B\to A$ be an arbitrary function, and define

$$
A+_{\mathcal{R}}B=\{a+b:a\in A,\ b\in B,\ a\ne\mathcal{R}(b)\}.
$$

**Small-set restricted-sumset conjecture.** If

$$
|A|+2|B|\leqslant p,
$$

then

$$
|A+_{\mathcal{R}}B|\geqslant |A|+|B|-3.
$$

This extends the matching case to arbitrary functions, allowing repeated forbidden partners. The paper identifies this regime as open; its main results prove related bounds under stronger quantitative hypotheses.

367549.title: The boundedness conjecture for gluing posets
367549.literal_statement: Let $\mathcal P_1$ and $\mathcal P_2$ be finite posets with bounded saturation number, and let $\mathcal P_2*\mathcal P_1$ denote their gluing, obtained by placing every element of $\mathcal P_1$ below every element of $\mathcal P_2$. Let $\operatorname{sat}^*(n,\mathcal P)$ denote the induced saturation number. **Gluing-boundedness conjecture.** The glued poset $\mathcal P_2*\mathcal P_1$ also has bounded saturation number. This is a special case of the preceding unboundedness conjecture and is presented as a desired extension of the paper's boundedness theorem to arbitrary posets.

367669.title: Generic small-time null-controllability conjecture for the heat equation on graphs
367669.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a graph with $N$ edges $(e_i)_{i=1,\dots,N}$ and let $\omega$ be an open subset of $\mathcal{G}$. The lengths of the edges are $(\ell_i)_{i=1,\dots,N}$.

**Generic heat-control conjecture.** Generically with respect to the lengths $(\ell_i)_{i=1,\dots,N}$, the heat equation is small-time null-controllable.

The claim is presented as a natural extension of the stated result for generic star graphs, where small-time null-controllability holds for every $T>0$. Its validity for more general graph structures remains open.
